summary: amis widget package fetches remote shell payload and exfiltrates host metadata to hardcoded IP
details: The package ships dist/bsrc-loader.js, invoked via the declared renderer entry dist/renderer.umd.js (require('./bsrc-loader.js!./payload.txt')). On Linux hosts, after a Baidu-internal SSRF probe at http://bsrc-ssrf.n.baidu-int.com succeeds, the loader spawns /bin/sh -c with a payload that curls/wgets http://49.232.169.67:80/slt and pipes the response to a shell, executing arbitrary remote code fetched over plaintext HTTP from a bare IP. On every loader invocation it also base64url-encodes process.cwd(), the webpack rootContext/context/resourcePath, pid, and the SSRF probe response body, and sends the bundle as a query string to http://49.232.169.67:43817/bsrc-r268. The destination IP is assembled from an octet array (['49','232','169','67'].join('.')) and a marker constant BSRC_RCE_R268_f9137a is present. The package description self-labels as 'Authorized AI Suda webpack inline-loader validation'; the behavior is remote fetch-and-execute plus host-context exfiltration to a hardcoded bare-IP endpoint.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
